names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 10 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Codrat».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Μαρτίου, «Άγιοι Κοδράτος, Ανεκτός, Παύλος, Διονύσιος, Κυπριανός και Κρήσκης», with the rank word left off.

floruit.note: doxologia.ro opens the life «Pe vremea lui Deciu (249-251) și a lui Valerian (253-259) s-a născut Sfântul Mucenic Codrat». The bounds are the two reigns the page prints; it gives no year for the martyrdom, only that it fell on 10 March.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Codrat»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Κοδράτος, Ανεκτός, Παύλος, Διονύσιος, Κυπριανός και Κρήσκης»

attestations.note: The page enumerates the six friends and puts their martyrdom at Corinth «κατά τον διωγμό των αυτοκρατόρων Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.) ή Ουαλεριανού (253-259 μ.Χ.)», under the governor of Greece Jason, leaving the choice of persecution open. It quotes the Menologion of Basil II for Quadratus's birth in the mountains and gives Dionysius a paragraph of his own, in which he is stabbed with a knife rather than beheaded. It prints a distich for each pair of them and gives no year.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Codrat, Ciprian, Dionisie și al celor împreună cu dânșii, glasul 4. The page prints the common of martyrs for all of them together, with the reading «nesctricăciunii».

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contests received from you, our God, the crowns of incorruption. For having your strength, they overthrew the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἐξάριθμος χορός, τῶν Χριστοῦ Ἀθλοφόρων, ὑμνείσθω εὐσεθῶς, μελωδίαις ᾀσμάτων, Κοδράτος καὶ Ἄνεκτος, Παῦλος καὶ Διονύσιος, καὶ σὺν Κρήσκεντι, Κυπριανὸς ὁ θεόφρων τὴν Τριάδα γάρ, διηνεκῶς δυσωπούσιν, ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ, on the page of Άγιοι Κοδράτος, Ανεκτός, Παύλος, Διονύσιος, Κυπριανός και Κρήσκης. It names all six. The page prints a second apolytikion in Ἦχος δ’, «Ὁ Μάρτυς σου Κύριε», which is the common of a single martyr and names nobody; it is not taken. The page's «εὐσεθῶς» for «εὐσεβῶς» is the reading it prints.

english.text: Let the six-numbered choir of the victory-bearers of Christ be hymned in piety with melodies of song — Quadratus and Anectus, Paul and Dionysius, and with Crescens, Cyprian of godly mind; for they entreat the Trinity without ceasing for our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς λαμπάς ἑξάφωτος ἐν τῇ Κορίνθῳ, καρτερῶς ἀθλήσαντες, ὤφθητε Μάρτυρες σοφοί, φωταγωγοῦντες ταῖς χάρισι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἀπαύστως τό πλήρωμα.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον, on the same page, which keeps the six together as one lamp of six lights at Corinth.

english.text: Like a lamp of six lights at Corinth you were seen, wise martyrs, contending with endurance and lighting up the fullness of the Church unceasingly with your graces.
